chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Sayf ibn Amira, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to Mufaddal ibn Umar: 'O Mufaddal! If you wish to know whether a man is wretched or fortunate, look at his generosity and his kindness, to whom he directs them. If he directs them to those who are their rightful recipients, then know that he is destined for goodness; but if he directs them to those who are not their rightful recipients, then know that there is no goodness for him with Allah.'

key_terms.أَهْلُهُ: Those who are rightful or deserving recipients
key_terms.شَقِيٌّ: Wretched, unfortunate, or doomed to hell

ai.seo_question: How can one determine if a person is spiritually fortunate or wretched based on their charity?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) instructs Muaffal ibn Umar that true felicity is determined not merely by the act of giving, but by the discernment of *ahluhu* (those truly deserving of one's kindness). This criterion emphasizes the Shia scholarly emphasis on *adab al-sadaqah* (etiquette of charity), where directing benevolence to the worthy ensures spiritual reward, while misdirected generosity may indicate a lack of divine favor.
